audience.text: Python developers building applications that require generating Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code barcodes without system-level dependencies.

capabilities.text: Supports Code 128, Code 39 (base and Extended), EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code (Model 2) via dedicated helpers or `generate()`.
capabilities.title: Generate multiple barcode symbologies

capabilities.text: Produce SVG via `to_svg()` and PNG via `to_png()`, with optional `RenderOptions` for scale, DPI, module width, colors, and text display.
capabilities.title: Render to SVG and PNG

capabilities.text: Control scale, DPI, module width/height, quiet zone, foreground/background color, transparent background, and text display via `RenderOptions`.
capabilities.title: Customize rendering with RenderOptions

capabilities.text: Implement or use built-in `SvgRenderer`, `PngRenderer`, or `PdfRenderer` subclasses and pass them to `Barcode.render()`.
capabilities.title: Support custom renderers

capabilities.text: Use `Code128Options`, `Code39Options`, `Ean13Options`, `Ean8Options`, `UpcaOptions`, `UpceOptions`, and `QrOptions` to control encoding behavior.
capabilities.title: Configure symbology-specific options

capabilities.text: Raise `BarcodeError`, `EncodingError`, `InvalidInputError`, `RenderingError`, `SymbologyNotFoundError`, `UnsupportedCapabilityError`, and `UnsupportedFeatureError` for distinct failure modes.
capabilities.title: Handle errors with typed exceptions

limitations.text: PDF rendering is not implemented; `Barcode.to_pdf()` and `PdfRenderer.render()` raise `NotImplementedError`.
ECI normalization and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions` exposing `eci_assignment_number`.
GS1 data parsing and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions` exposing `gs1_enabled`.

problems_solved.text: Provides a pure-Python, dependency-light way to generate multiple barcode symbologies with deterministic output.
Enables flexible barcode rendering to SVG and PNG formats with configurable options like scale, DPI, module width, and text display.
Supports both dedicated helper functions and a generic `generate()` entry point for selecting symbologies by name.

product_summary.text: Aspose.BarCode FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for generating deterministic, standards-compliant linear and 2D barcodes.

uncertainties: The exact set of symbologies supported beyond those explicitly listed in examples and public symbols is unclear.
Whether `PdfRenderer` is partially implemented or only stubbed is not evident from available symbols.
The behavior of `ResolvedRenderOptions` when applied is not described beyond its existence.
The scope of `aspose_barcode_foss._internal` and its stability is not documented.
Whether `BarcodeError` and its subclasses are raised in all documented error conditions is not confirmed.
The versioning scheme and compatibility guarantees for the FOSS build are not stated.
The exact dependency on Pillow for PNG rendering and whether it is optional for SVG-only use is not clarified beyond the declared requirement.
Whether custom `Renderer` implementations beyond the provided ones are tested or supported is not stated.

workflows.name: Generate and render a Code 128 barcode
workflows.text: Call `code128()` with payload, then invoke `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to produce output.

workflows.name: Generate a QR Code with custom options
workflows.text: Use `qr()` with payload and `QrOptions` specifying error correction level and encoding mode, then render to PNG.

workflows.name: Render with custom options
workflows.text: Pass `RenderOptions` to `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to control scale, DPI, module width, and text display.

workflows.name: Render using a specific renderer
workflows.text: Instantiate a `SvgRenderer` or `PngRenderer`, pass it to `Barcode.render()` with `RenderOptions`, and extract rendered data.

workflows.name: Select symbology generically
workflows.text: Call `generate()` with symbology name and payload to produce a barcode object for any supported type.

workflows.name: Add check digit to Code 39
workflows.text: Use `code39()` with `Code39Options(add_check_digit=True)` to encode payload with modulo-43 check character.
